sections.heading: C2 — Fitness, vision, fatigue and impairment
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Fitness, vision, fatigue and impairment

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
The staged handbook says buying, consuming or possessing alcohol is prohibited below age 21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
According to the staged manual, driving with BAC of 0.08% or above can result in arrest. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
For a driver younger than 21, the handbook also states arrest is possible at BAC 0.02%. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
BAC expresses the percentage of alcohol in blood; the manual lists breath, blood and urine testing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
The manual says refusing a BAC test requested by a police or traffic officer can cost a driver the license for one year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
For a first DWI conviction, the source states fines and court costs apply and jail is possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
The first-conviction description also requires treatment and installation of an ignition-interlock device. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes MVD as having authority to revoke the driver’s license after DWI. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A01
The source says later DWI convictions increase fines, jail time and the length of license revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A01
The handbook states that a DWI conviction stays on the driving record for 25 years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes driving under any drug’s influence that makes driving unsafe as unlawful. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
The medical-reporting text requires periodic physician-signed medical statements to MVD for drivers with epilepsy, diabetes, adverse heart conditions or other medical problems. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
The source directs readers to MVD for further information about those medical-reporting requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
The epilepsy paragraph calls for frequent checkups, careful medicine management and six months stable and seizure-free before license issuance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A02
For insulin-treated diabetes, the source cautions against driving when an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A02
The insulin paragraph identifies missed food or an incorrect insulin amount as possible causes of the described reaction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A02
While a doctor adjusts insulin dosage, the manual suggests another person driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A02
The diabetes guidance recommends regular eye examinations for night blindness and other vision difficulties. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A02
The heart paragraph cautions people with heart disease, high blood pressure, circulation problems or blackout, fainting or heart-attack risk against driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A02
A patient seeing a doctor for a heart condition should ask whether it can affect safe driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A02
Strong worry, excitement, fear, anger or depression can interfere with driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A02
If angry or excited, allow time to calm down and remain off the road until calm. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A02
When worried or upset, the handbook emphasizes keeping attention on driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A02
Dialing or talking on a mobile phone can dangerously distract a driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A02
Where possible, pull to the roadside before making or receiving a phone call. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A02
The source notes that some towns prohibit phone use while driving without a hands-free device; it does not identify the towns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0033]

verification_debt.claim_text: Page32 alcohol age restrictions, BAC arrest figures, refusal consequences, DWI penalties/interlock/revocation and25-year record period require current official/legal review. Arrest possibility is not guilt, and no unprinted exceptions, offense categories, fine amounts, forms or hearing deadlines are invented.

Page33 physician statements and epilepsy/diabetes/heart-condition guidance, including six months seizure-free, are source descriptions only. Current MVD requirements and clinician review are required before teaching or treating them as individual fitness advice. No reporting frequency, form name or blanket personal medical clearance is inferred.
Page33 gives unspecified-town hands-free restrictions, not a current statewide legal rule or a claim hands-free use is safe. Verify present applicable local/state law before release.
Page33 says some find radio listening helpful when upset. This optional observation is not indexed as a safe distraction remedy; current attention/safety review remains pending.
